look_here_first: Usually an arching shrub or scrambling vine. Start at a TERMINAL flowering shoot: pale 2-lipped relatively short flowers, usually 17–20 mm, with connate/perfoliate terminal floral bracts. A leaf pair fused beneath the inflorescence does NOT prove coral honeysuckle; both share it.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Shrubby, arching or scrambling growth; leafy stems opposite, simple, usually short-petiolate; upper fused terminal bracts possible.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Opposite simple leaves with entire to near-entire margins; petiole lengths and fused terminal bracts vary by species.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Cream or white short clearly two-lipped corollas usually about 17–19.5 mm long in condensed terminal inflorescences; petals fused into corolla; calyx sits above inferior ovary.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Red-orange to scarlet berries about 6.5–10 mm; fruit color does not separate from coral honeysuckle.
